body: The panic/crash is a debug feature caused by the debug tracing you've enabled. Without that it would try to just heal the inconsistency. That said, there is an inconsistency and there shouldn't be...

Wow. Thank you!

I don't yet have a clue why it's happening, but what is happening is that in a single batch of local file updates, we get the same file twice. We then twice remove the original file from before the update, and add the first and second file.

I do believe it's a bug that we get the same file twice in one batch, but I also think we should handle that case. Because for remote devices I think that can happen legitimately, so we should be able handle it in db. Lots of "I think"s in there, need to investigate :)

So the same file twice could be done by rename detection, as it marks the file as deleted twice most likely, because we don't have dirty read support.

I was under the impression that should not be an issue

Sounds plausible, the file is 0 bytes long so likely match for any other created 0 byte long file...

I guess the problem is our non-dirty-read transactions. We create a new item and sequence entry, dropping the old sequence entry. Then we get the next instance, create a new item and sequence entry but can't find the intermediate sequence entry we created.

Ok, then that's the problem. When we insert the same file twice, the first gets sequence A, second sequence B. We delete the old sequence entry, create a new one from A pointing at the file, then create a second one from B to the file and overwrite the file entry with sequence B. Thus the entry for sequence A is still there, pointing at a file with sequence B.
Maybe we should skip rename detection for zero byte files, too :)
I'll propose a solution to the general "file present more than once in a to-be-update list", separate from the zero bytes and other rename stuff that can potentially also be improved/fixed.

If len(blocks) == 0 goto fail

I guess having a block for an empty file is a very old thing, but I can't think of a good reason why we need it.
Yeah I had the same trip down memory lane. To begin with we didn't have a separate size field, I think, and it's still a protocol error for a file not to have blocks.
